born Lewisham 31 January 1936; 5:36:14 in his first London-Brighton, fastest by an Englishman (1960); joined Belgrave July 1948 aged 12; Junior Team Manager; won the L.C.C. Junior Mile 1953; won the 1954 Wimbledon 5¾ miles road trial in record 28:24; tuberculosis 1955, discharged from National Service on 100% disability pension; fully fit again by end of 1959; fastest time on the Redhill stage of the London-Brighton Relay; 2nd Darlington to Barnard Castle 16½ 1960; club record 1:51:19 in the Belgrave '20' 1960; 2nd S.L.H. '30' 1960 in 2:56:03; 3rd London-Brighton 1960; fastest Redhill stage London-Brighton Relay 1960; won Isle of Man T.T. course race 1961 in record; 78th National 1962 at Blackpool; 7th Wigmore 15 and 10th Finchley 20 1962; ran 1962 Comrades Marathon for R.R.C. team that placed 1st, 3rd, 4th and 5th; 12th Poly Marathon 1962; won Belgrave '20' 1962 in 1:48:50; 8th A.A.A. Marathon 1962 in 2:31:30; won Harry Parker Memorial Bowl; retired 1964 and became an athletics photographer; married Jill 1969

photos.c:
Some interesting styles in baton changing at the 100 x 1 mile relay.
Top left. Kevin Clarke (83) demonstrates the cross leg shuffle as he takes the baton from new member L.Lyons.
Top right. M.Harrison (13) demonstrates the walkers change as he hands over to P.Moysey.
Bottom left. Steve Webb (69) milkman to the last gives Pat Lyttle no change.
Centre. Ian Morton (75) provides a fine example of the jumping high level pass with Graham Allerton intercepting.
Bottom right. Colin Pearson (84) uses the jumping low level pass to send Tony Fairclough on his way.
The one man club team. Pat Lyttle who defeated 2 clubs single handed in a Rossenheim League match.
The one man club team. Pat Lyttle who defeated 2 clubs single handed in a Rossenheim League match.

TEAM SPIRIT

Tremendous team spirit has been a key feature off all the British League fixtures this year. When Pat Lyttle put in his best performance to date in winning the 'B' string 100m and 200m at the Warley meeting the first to congratulate him was jumps Captain Derrick Williams. This picture records Derricks only moment of inactivity as he amassed 30 points from; High Jump, Long Jump, Triple Jump, 100m and 400m Relay Squads.

Our victorious team after their outstanding win in the Wellington Relays held on the race course at Ostend.
Back row left to right; Mike Alleyne, Derrick Williams, Guy Sagar, Pat Lyttle, Dave Mote, Gary Staines, John Gladwin, Kevin Sturman, Richard Addison, and Mark Sinclair.
Front row left to right; Paul Richley, Stuart Paton, Oliver Foote, and Team Manager - Leo Coy.
Pat Lyttle heads the field at the first takeover in the British League Match 3 which we won so convincingly at Windsor.

PHOTOS FROM THE CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS

Joe Minetti (33) completes a sprint double by winning the 200m from Stuart Paton who clocked a nippy 22.9 - not bad for a middle distance man! Others in shot , left to right, are Mike Scott, Andy Paton, Phil Smith and Pat Lyttle

Gordon Biscoe appears to be looking at the watch in disbelief but it was a comfortable 58 at the bell for Richard O'Hara who ran out an easy winner. Alan Painter, a youngster of 39, was the only other runner inside 2 minutes. Pat Lyttle is still in touch at this point but his legs are about to part company with the rest of his body any second!

Front page photo by Mark Shearman. It's a silver medal for 800 metre racer Tom Lerwill at the World Junior Championships in Sydney. Nineteen year-old Tom reduced his best ever time to 1:47.27 when chasing home the Kenyan Kimutai in his semi-final, and then in the final ran with great tactical awareness to work his way through the field, moving into second place in the home stretch.

Apart from his exploits in individual 800m events, Tom Lerwill had a part to play in two of our 4x400m records of 1996. In Istanbul he joined Ridgeon, Rawlinson and Nolan for a 3:09.30 clocking and pictured above, he anchored our under 20 squad to a 3:17.1 National Junior League record with a 47.6 effort.

photos.c: The tall figure of Jason Lobo —800 metre action at the Bukit Jalil Stadium, Kuala Lumpur.

Left: Jason Lobo leads the Gold Cup 1500 metres mid-way through the race. He eventually placed 2nd to Kevin McKay (Sale) pictured here close up behind the Belgrave man. Jason finished the season with best 1998 performances of 49.6/ 1:47.48/3:48.90 for 400m through 1500m.

1. One of the most glorious sights in athletics is the start of the Senior Men's National Cross Country Championships. Half a mile into the 2000 race at Stowe School, Buckinghhamshire, and the field is led by Belgrave's Paul Evans with Paul Freary just behind him and to the right. On the left, behind 2516 is Kevin Nash and next but one above 2321 is Rob McHarg. On the right, behind the orange vested .24 is Jason Lobo, making a more conservative start, with Lee Hurst next but one on the left of .24. In the centre, just behind and to the right of the Blackheath vest is Alaster Stewart and next on the right, with only his claret bandana showing is Charles Herrington. That's eight in the top 100 and they spent the next half mile gaining even more forward positions. You might have to take the Editor's word for this one: on the skyline just to the left of the tree can be seen Phil Carstairs' thinning thatch. Will Cockerell has also been picked out in this vicinity by one viewer - but blowed if we can find him now!
Jason Lobo finds himself under attack from Alaster Stewart, running one of his last races for Redhill Runners before moving to Wimbledon and joining the Bels.
Below: Ignoring the pouring rain at the end of the race. Lee Hurst, Paul Freary, Spencer Barden, Jason Lobo, Paul Evans and Mark Miles.

Right: An hour before "National" race time. Bill Laws and John Jeffery have driven back to Milton Keynes to pick up Paul Evans whose car has broken down, leaving the rest of the team to pose for the pre-race photo. Back row: Eric Hall (President), Don Anderson, Paul Coughlan, Alan Mead, Alaster Stewart, Paul Freary, Jason Lobo, Kevin Nash, Phil Carstairs, Rob Harding. Front: Darryl Ochse, Will Cockerell, Charles Herrington, Lee Hurst, Rob McHarg.

Above: Irish eyes were not the only ones smiling when the the Belgrave team collected their prizes in Wallace Park. Rob McHarg, Paul Freary, Alaster Stewart, Yacin Yusuf (crouching), Jason Lobo and Spencer Barden enjoy being Irish Road Relay Champions.
